subject: Urgent: VitalBridge production 429s and severe throughput drop
messages:
From: Darren Cole <darren.cole@vitalbridge.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: lydia.park@vitalbridge.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production errors: sudden 429 surge + throughput drop

Naomi —

We're seeing a sudden spike in 429 responses across our production traffic since 07:40 PDT this morning. Latency also climbed (p95 from ~180ms to ~1200ms) and overall throughput has dropped ~60%. This coincides exactly with the time our rollout of the new inference pipeline started.

Key details:
- Sample request IDs: req_7a9c, req_7a9d, req_7a9f (included in attached CSV).
- Errors are 429 with payload: "rate_limit_exceeded" and occasional 503s.
- We are not hitting the usage numbers we expected on our side; this looks enforcement-side.

This is blocking our client demo later today and Finance/Procurement are escalating — they want an explanation and a mitigation plan (they included procurement@vitalbridge.com).

Can you confirm whether VitalBridge has had an unexpected quota/burst credit drain or if there was a policy change? We need a temporary bypass or higher burst allowance to keep the rollout alive.

Attached: vitalbridge_error_dashboard.png and request_ids_07021.csv

Thanks,
Darren
Director, Platform Operations
VitalBridge Health

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
To: Darren Cole <darren.cole@vitalbridge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors: sudden 429 surge + throughput drop

Darren — thank you for the signal and the artifacts, I see the dashboard screenshot and the sample request ids. Sorry you're hitting this during a rollout — we'll prioritize.

Immediate steps I'm initiating:
1) Looping in Marissa (CS lead) and Karthik (policy/traffic) to coordinate with runtime/ops.
2) Asking ops to verify if VitalBridge's burst credits were exhausted or if a new rate-window rule applied at 07:40.
3) If that's the root cause, we will provision a time-limited burst override (1 hour) and follow with a controlled quota increase while we triage.

Can you confirm the rollout window and whether you can put the rollout into a reduced concurrency mode for 30 minutes if we apply a burst override? That will reduce risk of re-saturating while we investigate.

I'll update within 20 minutes.

Best,
Naomi
Account Director — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: request_ids_07021.csv]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Darren Cole <darren.cole@vitalbridge.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors: sudden 429 surge + throughput drop

Adding an operational update and next actions.

Summary of what's happening (ops triage findings):
- Observed pattern: tenant-level burst credits reached zero at ~07:41 PDT and the burst safety valve kicked in. That caused aggressive shedding (manifested as 429s) plus downstream queueing which increased p95 latency and reduced throughput.
- No emergency policy rollouts were executed in the last 24h; this appears to be a credit depletion combined with a conservative burst-window enforcement.

Planned mitigation (immediate):
1) Ops will apply a temporary burst override for VitalBridge (2x burst capacity) for a 60-minute window starting now.
2) Engineering will disable the strict safety valve for that tenant's queue while we replay the request samples in a staging canary.
3) Karthik will follow up on policy adjustments to prevent immediate retriggering; we will preserve audit logs for compliance.

Longer-term ask:
- We should offer VitalBridge a short-term credit compensation for the hours where their rollout was impacted (finance to advise).
- Recommend we review their quota profile and bump the baseline token allowance for the next 30 days while they finish the rollout.

I will email ops and the runtime lead now and keep Darren posted. Naomi — can you capture the procurement ask (billing annotation/credit) and loop finance if needed?

Marissa
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: temporary_burst_plan.md]
From: Darren Cole <darren.cole@vitalbridge.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: lydia.park@vitalbridge.com, procurement@vitalbridge.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 16:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors: sudden 429 surge + throughput drop

Thank you — the temporary burst override reduced the 429s and latency returned to normal within ~12 minutes of the change. We throttled the rollout concurrency as requested; no client-facing impact beyond the delayed demo.

Procurement has asked for a short note documenting the window, the cause (burst credit exhaustion + safety valve), and the make-good plan (credit or invoice adjustment). Can someone from Finance/CS provide that note and a point of contact? We're preparing a brief for our leadership call tomorrow.

Appreciate the quick response. Please keep me posted on the policy follow-up and any permanent quota changes.

Best,
Darren
Director, Platform Operations
VitalBridge Health
